summary: The honeynet's short-term memory tree shows several inconsistencies and potential deception signals across hosts, ports, files, vulnerabilities, and traps.
issues: Port 443 on edge-fw has an impossible banner for the service https.
File /etc/ssl/private/server.key on edge-fw is referenced by a vulnerability but does not match the expected service.
File /etc/passwd.bak on edge-fw does not fit the parent port/service for SSH.
File /etc/backup/config_backup.conf on bastion-01 is referenced by a vulnerability but does not match the expected service.
File /var/www/html/admin_credentials.txt on bastion-01 does not fit the parent port/service for HTTP.
File /etc/ops/secret_keys.json on jump-ops is referenced by a vulnerability but does not match the expected service.
File /var/www/html/api_keys.txt on dmz-api-01 is referenced by a vulnerability but does not match the expected service.
File /var/www/html/operations_backup.zip on jump-ops does not fit the parent port/service for HTTP.
Trap loops on hosts do not point to existing files, indicating potential deception.
Credential chains do not loop attackers back to the starting point, suggesting a flaw in the deception strategy.
